X-Rid Travel Trailer Is Equipped for Complete Off-Grid Autonomy and Has a Self-Sustaining Shell
14 photos
Photo: LifeStyle Camper
While the United States has one of the largest RV and camper scenes in the world, there are other countries that produce some very capable options. Today, we travel to Ukraine where we find a completely autonomous camper, ‘autonomous’ in the sense that you can indulge in total off-grid living and even light off-road use.
It’s called the X-Rid, no “G,” and currently, it stands as LifeStyle Camper’s total off-grid camping solution. As such, I felt it would be a great idea to run through this beast and see what it has in store for us.
Photo: LifeStyle Camper First and foremost, allow me to point out that the X-Rid is said to start off at around €29,000, or around $32,500, so quite a hefty price by RV standards all around the world. I mean, in the US, you can unlock a camper that has room for as many as eight people at half that price. Still, there are clear reasons why the X-Rid is priced as such.
One of the most important reasons isn’t necessarily the off-grid and off-road systems in place – we'll get to those – but rather, how the shell is built. According to the manufacturer’s website, we’re looking at a composite and self-supporting body composed of sandwich panels with foam core.
While the manufacturer doesn’t make a mention of it, it appears that aluminum extrusions are used to hold those panels in place. If you look closely at the images in the gallery, you can see the edges that line the body
Photo: LifeStyle Camper But, on top of it all, LifeStyle adds a layer of bed liner, enclosing the entire shell in a waterproof and seamless coat. This, however, does not mean that this one is bulletproof in any way; the seams created by windows, cargo bay hatches, the rear door that encloses the kitchen, and any vents or AC units do need to be checked on regularly.
That shell is then placed on top of a steel chassis with running gear provided by Knott, a big name over in Europe, and providing an independent suspension setup with springs and shocks. It’s rated for a peak of 1,500 kg (3,307 lbs) and a standard X-Rid can weigh as little as 1,000 kg (2,205 lbs).
Some wood does make it into the X-Rid, but from what I can see it’s all hidden underneath the panels and inside the camper, so it’s safe from the elements in case the weather takes a turn for the worst. While moisture can be an issue inside campers, the X-Rid is rocking ample vents and windows to keep it dry.
Photo: LifeStyle Camper What I liked about the X-Rid is that it is a camper that is a bit different than most others out there, even though it houses a galley at the rear of this unit, much like a teardrop camper. Inside , LifeStyle adds a modular dinette that transforms into a bed for two guests (comfortably) at night, but the X-Rid is also larger enough to include an en-suite wet bath.
The lifestyle inside is also supported by ample storage along the upper edges of the cabin, a wardrobe across from the bathroom, TV, and curtains to give us some privacy when we wish for it.
Among all that, the manufacturer stuffs this unit full of features to keep us comfortable in the wildest of places. This includes ducted heating and cooling, but also hot water, Alpine audio system, lighting, ventilation, and most importantly, that off-grid system, granted by the one and only EcoFlow, a brand that has grown to be loved the world over for their systems.
Photo: LifeStyle Camper A Delta 3 Plus power station sits at the center of the abilities, along with two charge controllers and 370 W of solar on the roof.
Back outside, LifeStyle continues to equip the X-Rid with a very well-appointed kitchen, ready with a 70-liter fridge, sink/cooktop combo with flush countertop, ample storage, and a pass-through that allows the interior and kitchen to communicate with one another. Speakers are also in place to enjoy some tunes while cooking.
Given the size and strength of the X-Rid's body, we can also see an awning sticking off the side, perfect for setting up a little outdoor dining area and lounge – why not grab an annex – and on top, a rack system means we can add plenty of extra cargo. More cargo can be stuffed into the body itself via those hatches we see.
Photo: LifeStyle Camper Keep in mind that this is just the tip of the iceberg in terms of what the X-Rid has in store and just how much more it can be decked out in options and extras. This means that, if you’re in Europe and like what you see here, be sure to get in touch with LifeStyle for the full tour of their freshest camper.
If, however, you live in the US or anywhere other than Europe, you may have a very hard time getting your hands on this one. But, if you like what you see, at least you’ll know what to look for locally.
